title: Drugs – harm and consequences
intro: Islam forbids everything that harms the mind and body – and drugs do both.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says: O believers, intoxicants (khamr), gambling, idols and fortune-telling arrows are filthy things – the work of Shaytan – so stay away from them, so that you may be successful. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Ma’idah 5:90)</small>

A well-known principle of Islam is that it forbids everything that harms a person’s physical and mental health. Medicine and experience have shown that drugs harm the mind and the body, cause the illness of addiction, and lead to bad and even criminal behaviour. So the conclusion is clear: using drugs, in any amount, is strictly forbidden (haram) in Islam.
Drugs are substances that make a person intoxicated (“high”) and unable to think clearly. Narcotics – the name for all kinds of drugs – are clearly forbidden in Islam because of the harm they do.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: When asked about certain forbidden drinks, the Prophet (SAW) said: “Every intoxicant is khamr, and every khamr is haram.” (Muslim) Explaining what khamr is, he also said: “Khamr is whatever clouds the mind.” (Bukhari)

The wide use of drugs in the world today is a great evil. Islam teaches that it is haram – a major sin – whose results are felt in this world and in the akhirah. In this world, drug use harms every part of society, and most of all the user and their family.

items: harm to your own health and your family’s health,
harm to the mental and physical health of children,
losing the family’s money and belongings,
getting into a criminal world that is very hard to leave,
crime, and punishment by the law.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: …and do not throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:195)</small>

Whoever starts down this bad road by trying drugs has taken the first step towards addiction. Life is a gift from Allah (SWT), and we must look after it as He guides us. Harming our body, life, mind, children or belongings is a misuse of the freedom He gave us.
We don’t know the details of the punishment in the akhirah, but we know for sure that sincere repentance (tawbah) wipes away sins and so lessens the punishment.

Modern laws mostly focus on treatment, but Islamic teaching pays much more attention to prevention – stopping drug use before it ever becomes an illness. If someone does become addicted, they have a duty to get treatment. Addiction makes a person keep using again and again, and usually only proper medical treatment in special centres can stop it.

learn.title: ⚠️ Be careful
learn.html: A dealer may try to give you drugs to “try” for free. Later they will make you pay a lot for every dose – just to make money, and to destroy your life. Say no, walk away, and tell a parent, your teacher or another adult you trust.

The spread of drugs is a price people pay for weakening faith and spirituality, breaking Allah’s rules and not caring about life – wanting pleasure and to “try everything”. When people understand the causes and start to respect faith and Allah’s commands again, it will be easier to deal with this and similar problems.

practice.title: Saying no
practice.prompt: Someone offers you something to “try”. Tap every good response, then tap Check.

options.text: 🙅 Say a clear “No, thanks” and walk away
👨‍👩‍👧 Tell a parent or another adult you trust
👫 Stay with friends who also say no

options.why: Trying is the first step towards addiction – and Islam forbids drugs in any amount.

options.text: 🤐 Keep it secret so nobody gets in trouble
options.why: Telling a trusted adult protects you and others.

items.text: Medicine a doctor gives you, used the way the doctor says
Trying a “free” drug from a stranger

options: Substances that make a person intoxicated and unable to think clearly

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) say khamr is?
How much of a drug is allowed?
options: None – it is haram in any amount

questions.q: What does Islamic teaching focus on most?
options: Prevention – stopping it before it starts

questions.q: What should a person who is addicted do?
Why might a dealer give drugs for free at first?
options: So you get addicted and pay a lot later

practice.title: Questions, tasks and talking with your teacher
prompts: 📖 Why are drugs forbidden for Muslims?
💊 In which case may a Muslim use a drug-like medicine? Talk about medicine a doctor gives for treatment.
🏠 How does drug use harm a person, a family and a community?
🔍 Task: find out and explain with examples what the results of drug use are.
🛡️ Talk with your teacher: how can we act early (prevention) and protect ourselves from drugs?
